findings.title: failsIf[10] and failsIf[11] carry an unguarded bare 'v2' token that collides with this artifact's version integer, tripping the subject's own failsIf[16]/[19] - and the same collision was mitigated everywhere else in the document, so the omission is internally inconsistent rather than a considered reading.
findings.measurement: The artifact's version integer is 2. failsIf[10] reads 'a D-002 platform list is invented rather than quoted from G10 occupancy v2 #$.platforms' and failsIf[11] reads 'platformsQuotedFromG10OccupancyV2 is not ORDERED-EQUAL to G10 occupancy v2 #$.platforms'. Both use the token 'v2' as a free-standing word, not stemmed onto an artifact name the way control-protocol-contract.v2 and anti-lockstep-contract.v7 are. failsIf[16] and failsIf[19] each state that the artifact fails if 'a basedOn.*.role, whatIsNotAuthored, or failsIf current-standing clause uses a bare version token that collides with this artifact's version integer'. failsIf is one of the three named scopes. The predecessor's Stage A sweep classified these exact two occurrences as bare tokens - its bareTokensFound records 'v2 (once in basedOn.g23OccupancyV2.role, twice in failsIf)' - and returned CLEAN only because v1's version integer was 1 and therefore did not collide.
findings.whyItIsWrong: The subject demonstrably treated this collision as real when it drafted v2, and then applied the fix to two of the three in-scope sites and to authorityClaim, but not to failsIf. The v1 to v2 diff is unambiguous: v2 removed the 'Not this artifact's version number' guard from basedOn.g21FixtureCorpusV1.role, which is a .v1 lineage that no longer collides, and added that guard to basedOn.g10OccupancyV2.role and basedOn.g23OccupancyV2.role, which are the v2 lineages that now do; authorityClaim's disclaimer was rewritten from 'relative to g21-fixture-corpus.v1' to 'relative to G10 occupancy v2, G23 occupancy v2, or control-protocol-contract.v2'. That is a deliberate, correct response to the version integer moving from 1 to 2. The two failsIf clauses reference the same G10 occupancy v2 lineage in the same words and received neither a guard nor a stemmed name. So on the subject's own operative reading of its own test - the reading evidenced by what it chose to guard - failsIf[10] and failsIf[11] are unguarded colliding bare tokens inside a scope failsIf[16] names, and the artifact meets its own declared failure condition.
findings.counterReadingConsidered: A narrower reading of 'bare version token' - a version token with no referent at all, as in basedOn.contractV7.role's 'does not apply v7' - would exempt 'G10 occupancy v2' because the lineage words 'G10 occupancy' supply the referent. Under that reading no in-scope token collides and there is no finding. I do not adopt it, for two reasons. First, the controlling precedent in this lineage is the predecessor's own sweep, which listed 'G10 occupancy v2' under bareTokensFound and rested its CLEAN verdict on the integer rather than on the referent. Second, the subject itself rejects the narrow reading by its conduct: if the lineage word were sufficient, the guards newly added to basedOn.g10OccupancyV2.role and basedOn.g23OccupancyV2.role and the rewritten authorityClaim disclaimer would all be unnecessary. The document cannot both need the guard in a basedOn role and not need it in a failsIf clause quoting the same lineage in the same words.
findings.whyMustFix: Three grounds. First, this is the subject's own failsIf, not an external standard - an artifact whose bytes meet a failure condition it declares about itself cannot be recorded as written, because a later remasurement reading failsIf[16] against these bytes would have to record the artifact as failed. Second, the defect sits in the one list whose entire purpose is to state the conditions under which this candidate is unsound, so an unapplied self-check there is worse than the same wording anywhere else in the document. Third, the duplication recorded at CLAUDE-ALHG-V2-S-1 shows the clause was appended rather than executed: v2 added a second verbatim copy of the version-token test while leaving the test unapplied to the two clauses sitting nine and ten positions above it. The sweep was transcribed, not run.
findings.remedy: Stem both tokens in failsIf[10] and failsIf[11] the way the document already stems every other cross-lineage reference - write 'harness.DR-G10.provider-conformance.ts-major-1.v2 #$.platforms', which is the path already pinned at basedOn.g10OccupancyV2.path and recordedInputs. That removes the bare token entirely and needs no guard. Adding the 'Not this artifact's version number' guard to the two clauses would also close the finding, but stemming is the form the rest of the document uses and leaves nothing for a later sweep to re-litigate.

findings.title: failsIf[19] is a byte-identical duplicate of failsIf[16], newly introduced in v2, so the twenty-entry failure list carries nineteen distinct conditions.
findings.measurement: failsIf[16] and failsIf[19] are the same string byte-for-byte: "a basedOn.*.role, whatIsNotAuthored, or failsIf current-standing clause uses a bare version token that collides with this artifact's version integer". They are the only duplicate pair in the list. The v1 to v2 diff shows failsIf[19] was added in v2 alongside failsIf[17] and failsIf[18], the two genuinely new clauses that encode the landed M-1 and M-2 remedies; failsIf[16] already existed in v1 unchanged.
findings.whyItIsWrong: failsIf is a normative enumeration of distinct failure conditions and is read positionally by successors and remasurements. A repeated clause states nothing the list did not already state, inflates the count from nineteen conditions to twenty entries, and gives a later reader two indices for one test with no way to tell which is authoritative. It also mildly corrupts the record of what v2 actually changed: two of the three clauses v2 appended are substantive, and the third is a copy.
findings.whyNotMustFix: The duplicate introduces no false proposition and closes no leftover. Both copies say the same true thing about what would make the artifact fail, and nothing downstream is measured off the entry count. The list's meaning is unchanged if the duplicate is deleted, which is the test I apply for SHOULD-FIX rather than MUST-FIX.
findings.whyShouldFix: It is a defect in a frozen normative list that a successor would inherit, and it is direct evidence bearing on CLAUDE-ALHG-V2-M-1: appending a second copy of the version-token self-check, in the same edit that left that self-check unapplied to failsIf[10] and failsIf[11], is what distinguishes an unrun sweep from a considered narrow reading. Fixing the duplicate and fixing M-1 are the same editing pass.
findings.remedy: Delete failsIf[19]. failsIf[16] already carries the clause verbatim and predates it.

decision: REJECT. Both predecessor MUST-FIXes are landed correctly and every mechanical claim in the document verifies against disk, but one MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX stand, and the acceptance rule admits neither. CLAUDE-ALHG-V2-M-1: failsIf[10] and failsIf[11] carry an unguarded bare 'v2' token colliding with this artifact's version integer, inside a scope the subject's own failsIf[16] and failsIf[19] name, at a version where the collision first became live - and the same collision was mitigated at every other in-scope site in the same edit, so the omission is an unrun sweep rather than a considered narrow reading.
